details:
SPACE GRAVEYARD – The Forgotten Heroes of Space

Project Overview

SPACE GRAVEYARD is an interactive, bilingual digital space museum developed by the Iva Star Girls team for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026.

Our project focuses on preserving and sharing the scientific and historical stories of space equipment left behind on the Moon and Mars. We believe that when a spacecraft's mission ends, its contributions to science should never be forgotten.

Our goal is to transform complex space exploration information into an accessible, engaging, and educational digital experience.

The Problem and Our Solution

NASA has accumulated decades of valuable scientific discoveries through space exploration. However, information about completed missions and abandoned equipment is often spread across multiple resources and can be difficult for younger audiences to understand.

SPACE GRAVEYARD addresses this challenge by bringing mission histories, scientific discoveries, archival imagery, and interactive learning activities together in one platform.

Users can explore two main collections:

  • Moon Archive: Featuring the Apollo 11 Eagle Lunar Module descent stage and its historical significance.
  • Mars Archive: Featuring Sojourner, Spirit, and Opportunity, including their discoveries, engineering challenges, and scientific legacies.

Each exhibit presents mission information through educational storytelling, timelines, important events, and visual resources.

A separate Still Exploring section introduces Voyager 1 as an active extended mission, helping users understand the difference between equipment left behind and spacecraft that continue exploring space.

Interactive Learning Experience

We designed SPACE GRAVEYARD to be more than a traditional information website.

Our Explorer Program includes four learning challenges, a 15-question space quiz, experience points (XP), achievement levels, and seven unlockable badges.

These features encourage users to explore mission stories, test their knowledge, and track their learning progress.

The platform supports both Turkish and English, making its educational content accessible to a wider international audience.

Technologies and Development

SPACE GRAVEYARD was developed using modern web technologies, including:

  • React: For building interactive user interfaces.
  • TypeScript: For structured and maintainable application development.
  • Vite: For efficient development and production builds.
  • Browser Local Storage: For saving user progress.
  • Responsive Web Design: For supporting desktop, tablet, and mobile experiences.

We also used AI-assisted development tools to support coding, debugging, and content preparation. Scientific information was reviewed using NASA's official resources.

The project uses NASA mission information and archival images, with source references provided to support scientific transparency.

Innovation and Creativity

Our project's originality comes from combining scientific storytelling, historical mission archives, bilingual education, and gamification into a single interactive digital museum.

Instead of simply listing facts about spacecraft, we focus on their complete journeys: why they were created, the challenges they faced, what they discovered, and the legacies they left behind.

We also distinguish between completed missions and continuing exploration, helping users develop a more accurate understanding of space science.

Target Audience and Expected Impact

SPACE GRAVEYARD is designed for middle school and high school students, teachers, and anyone interested in space exploration.

We aim to increase scientific curiosity, encourage independent research, improve understanding of space exploration history, and make NASA's scientific resources more approachable for younger generations.

The platform can also serve as a supplementary educational resource for classroom activities.

Future Development

Our next steps include expanding the mission archive, improving accessibility, developing additional educational activities, and conducting user testing to evaluate the learning experience.

Our vision is to create a digital home for the forgotten heroes of space, inspiring future generations through the discoveries of the past.

A mission may end, but its discoveries live on.
